analyst_view.overall: Inter (15th, 6 points) and Stuttgart (14th, 7 points) both want to climb towards the top eight. Inter drew 4-4 at Atalanta on Sunday after giving up three two-goal leads, with Pio Esposito scoring a hat-trick; Hakan Çalhanoğlu went off with a thigh injury there and is out (UEFA-based previews, Sports Mole and YSScores), and Bonny is out (counted), while Bastoni returns from a ban. New since the last view: La Gazzetta dello Sport (via Passioneinter) reports Lautaro Martínez will again start on the bench, with Esposito and Thuram up front and Lautaro aiming to start against Genoa on Saturday; Sports Mole still has him starting, so this rests on one report. Stuttgart drew 0-0 at Schalke; Stiller (groin, counted), Jaquez (rib) and Sauer are out and Demirović leads the line. French referee François Letexier (4.0 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already take Bonny off Inter and Stiller off Stuttgart (about -4% each), but they assume Lautaro and Çalhanoğlu. Çalhanoğlu, Inter's penalty and set-piece taker, is out, and one report (Gazzetta) says Lautaro only comes off the bench; with Esposito in form that is a mild cut, about 4%, to around 3.17. Before, I had Lautaro starting cancelling out Çalhanoğlu's absence; now both point the same way.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.1 corners, 6.2 of them Inter's, already up 6% for Inter's recent corner count. Dimarco and Spence are fit on the flanks and Stuttgart play wing-backs too, and losing Çalhanoğlu changes who takes the corners rather than how many, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.7 cards and already take a little off Inter for their quiet recent record and for referee Letexier, who sits near the average at 4.0 a game. Çalhanoğlu, who was one booking from a ban, won't play, and there is no rivalry, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.4 shots and already add about 20% to Inter's side for their recent shooting and take 7% off Stuttgart's. Inter at home with Esposito and Thuram should still shoot plenty, and Lautaro is expected to come on, so I stay at about 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, up 7% for Inter's accuracy lately and down 3% for Stuttgart's. Without Çalhanoğlu's long-range shooting and with Lautaro, Inter's best finisher, likely starting on the bench, I take a small 3% off, to about 10.3.
